response.sql:
WITH manager_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    p.player_id,
    COUNT(ma.player_id) AS award_count
  FROM player p
  LEFT JOIN manager_award ma ON p.player_id = ma.player_id
  GROUP BY p.player_id
),
total_awards AS (
  SELECT SUM(award_count) AS total_count
  FROM manager_counts
),
with_fractions AS (
  SELECT 
    mc.player_id,
    mc.award_count,
    CASE 
      WHEN ta.total_count IS NULL OR ta.total_count = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE CAST(mc.award_count AS NUMERIC) / ta.total_count
    END AS fraction
  FROM manager_counts mc
  CROSS JOIN total_awards ta
)
SELECT 
  player_id,
  award_count,
  fraction
FROM with_fractions
ORDER BY 
  CASE WHEN fraction IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
  fraction DESC,
  player_id
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A row is included for every player in the player table via LEFT JOIN to manager_award; players with no awards have award_count = 0
When total_count is NULL or 0, fractions are set to NULL (not calculated) but rows are still returned—an alternative reading of 'return nothing if that total is missing' would suppress all rows
The secondary sort by player_id breaks ties when fractions are equal; the request does not specify a tiebreaker

alternatives.interpretation: If 'return nothing if that total is missing' means return zero rows (not NULL fractions) when total_count is NULL or 0
alternatives.sql:
WITH manager_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    p.player_id,
    COUNT(ma.player_id) AS award_count
  FROM player p
  LEFT JOIN manager_award ma ON p.player_id = ma.player_id
  GROUP BY p.player_id
),
total_awards AS (
  SELECT SUM(award_count) AS total_count
  FROM manager_counts
)
SELECT 
  mc.player_id,
  mc.award_count,
  CAST(mc.award_count AS NUMERIC) / ta.total_count AS fraction
FROM manager_counts mc
CROSS JOIN total_awards ta
WHERE ta.total_count IS NOT NULL AND ta.total_count > 0
ORDER BY 
  fraction DESC,
  mc.player_id
LIMIT 10;
